precondition_evidence.DISCLOSURE_prior_knowledge: This amendment is NOT blind. A prior probe (recorded in NOTE-035) already measured that at +/-5 mm lateral offset PEAK jumps 145.88 -> 45.82 mm and STRONGEST_RETURN_CENTROID jumps by -101 mm, while LEADING_EDGE does not move. The author therefore knows, before writing S4, which candidates S4 is likely to eliminate. Two mitigations are recorded instead of pretending blindness: (a) S4 is justified as a defining property of a ranging instrument, not as a discriminator chosen for its outcome -- it would have been a defensible stage-2 check in the original preregistration and its absence there was an oversight; (b) the threshold is fixed by physics and not tuned: it is set at 5x the applied displacement, which sits two orders of magnitude above any continuous geometric response (<1 mm) and four times below the inter-path-family gap (~100 mm), so the verdict is insensitive to the exact multiple chosen. If a future reader judges this insufficient, the correct remedy is to re-run the selection on a scene the author has not probed, not to accept the result on trust.

offset_anchor_provenance.acquisition: separate session, sample interval 0.0624 s, not part of the 560 Edge Impulse recordings
offset_anchor_provenance.source: acquisition plot titles: 'Baseline', 'Shift left by 0.1 cm', 'Shift right by 0.1 cm'

payload.rationale: Stage 1+2 of the v0.1.0 preregistration left three survivors (PEAK, LEADING_EDGE, STRONGEST_RETURN_CENTROID), so the preregistered rule called for the stage-3 offset-anchor tie-break. Provenance recovery has now established what the anchors are and, in the same step, that they cannot serve as a tie-break for this scene model. Recovered (first-party, from the acquisition's own plot titles): the displacement is +/-0.1 cm (1 mm), the conditions are Baseline / 'Shift left by 0.1 cm' / 'Shift right by 0.1 cm'. NOT recovered: which body moved (sensor or bottle) -- the titles state no subject -- and any mounting/alignment metadata. Three independent reasons the anchors cannot discriminate: (1) magnitude -- the observed response is -7.62 / -9.80 mm, while the front-surface geometric response to a 1 mm lateral shift on a 28.5 mm radius cylinder is 28.5 - sqrt(28.5^2 - 1^2) = 0.018 mm, and the chord/refraction route through the bottle gives ~0.012 mm; the observation is 400-550x larger than any geometric prediction. (2) sign -- both directions decrease. A mirror-symmetric displacement of a mirror-symmetric scene cannot decrease range on both sides, so the real rig carried an unrecorded asymmetry (tilt, mounting, or an off-centre baseline). The simulated scene is mirror-symmetric and therefore cannot reproduce the pattern regardless of estimator. (3) resolution -- at the actual +/-1 mm displacement all three surviving candidates change by exactly 0.00 mm in simulation, below the 3.12 mm distance-bin width, so the anchors carry no discriminating information at the displacement that was actually used. Rather than pick an estimator without a criterion, this amendment adds S4: continuity of the range estimate under a small geometric perturbation. S4 is a defining property of a ranging instrument, on the same footing as S1 (geometric monotonicity) and S2 (gain invariance): an estimator whose output jumps discontinuously between path families is not measuring any single surface, and its value is then decided by Monte-Carlo sampling noise rather than by geometry.
payload.title: Add a physics-only continuity criterion (S4) to the distance-estimator preregistration, because the stage-3 offset anchors are not executable
